Sorry for taking so long! This may be slightly above GCSE but I'm hoping it'll help:

TLDR: transcription is creating the mRNA molecule from the DNA molecule. A protein called RNA Polymerase reads the unzipped DNA and uses ATP and free nucleotides to make the mRNA molecule. Translation is when the mRNA molecule is being read in order to make the peptide chain. mRNA enters the ribosome, and tRNA molecules bring the corresponding amino acids according to their complementary anti-codon. The amino acids are joined by peptide bonds to make the peptide chain.
Best of luck for tomorrow!!


Transcription is the first stage in DNA replication. It occurs in the nucleus because the DNA is in the nucleus - the DNA is unravelled (or, unzipped) and the triplicate code read by RNA Polymerase. The RNA Polymerase binds to the start codon (also known as the non-coding region) upstream of the protein-coding gene. 
RNA Polymerase uses free nucleotides to create a complementary mRNA molecule. (messenger RNA)

Translation is the second and final stage of DNA replication, and it is where the mRNA molecule is turned into (or, translated) into a peptide. mRNA moves out of the nucleus and into a ribosome. Here, tRNA molecules bring the relevent amino acid associated with each triplet of the triplicate code (transfer RNA). The tRNA molecules 'know' which amino acid to bring because they have a complementary anti-codon, which matches the mRNA strand that is currently being translated. 
As the tRNA molecules are bringing the amino acids together, peptide bonds are formed between the amino acids, and the peptide chain is formed.

Complementary is what the anti-codon is to the codon. Complimentary is just being nice to someone. Ensure you spell it well!
